questions.q: What is a UI Action, and where does it live?
options: A sys_ui_action record defining a button, form link, or context-menu item tied to a table
A sys_ui_policy record that reacts automatically to field value changes
A client script that only runs on form load
A table-level ACL that restricts who can view a record
questions.explain: UI Actions are configurable, click-triggered elements stored on sys_ui_action — unlike UI Policies, they don't fire automatically.

questions.q:
A UI Action's Condition field contains:

current.state == 6 && gs.hasRole('itil')

What determines whether a given user sees this button at all?
options: Both the record's state being 6 and the user holding the itil role must be true
The Condition field only runs once, at UI Action creation time
Only the user's role matters; state is ignored by the Condition field
This script controls what the button does when clicked, not whether it shows
questions.explain: The Condition field is a server-side script that must return true for the action to render — here that requires both the state check and the role check.

questions.q: What does the Client checkbox on a UI Action actually control?
options: Whether the Condition field is evaluated at all
Whether the action appears as a form button instead of a list choice
Whether the action's script runs client-side with g_form, or server-side with current after postback
Whether the UI Action is scoped to a custom application
questions.explain: Client checked means the script runs in the browser against g_form; unchecked means it runs server-side against current, like a Business Rule.

options: Navigates the user back to the updated record once the server-side script finishes
Sends the record's sys_id to a client-side g_form variable
Reloads the UI Action's own configuration record
Cancels the current.update() call that just ran
questions.explain: setRedirectURL(url) is the common server-side method for sending the user somewhere after the action runs — passing a record redirects to that updated record.

questions.q: A UI Action only needs to validate that a field is filled in on the form in front of the user, with no database write required. Which configuration fits best, and why?
options: Client unchecked, using current, since all validation must happen server-side
Client checked, but the script must still use current instead of g_form
Neither — this can only be done with a Business Rule
Client checked, using g_form directly, to avoid an unnecessary round trip to the server
questions.explain: When the action only needs to read or adjust what's already on the rendered form, keeping it client-side with g_form avoids a needless server round trip.
